$comment: Context budgets for Accessibility Agents, checked by
skills/a11y-core/scripts/measure-context.mjs --check budgets.json.
always_on_total_max is a ceiling: it starts at the 2026-09-21 measurement
plus five percent so the tree passes today and fails the moment cost
regresses. Lower it as each phase removes a legacy surface.
always_on_current_target is the Phase 6 end state for the standard package
alone. It is reported as a note, not a failure, until the legacy trees are
gone and the ceiling can be dropped onto it.
Numbers are chars/4 token estimates from estimateTokens() in that script.
Phase 1 (2026-09-21) lowered every ceiling onto the post-migration
measurement plus five percent. docs/context-baseline-2026-09.json holds the
pre-migration numbers; docs/context-after-phase-1.json holds these.
Phase 6 (2026-09-21) removed every legacy tree, so the ceiling is now the
standard package alone plus ten percent headroom. The Codex target is higher
than the others because Codex lists user-invocable skills in its catalog,
which the other clients do not; 63 entries at roughly 95 characters is the
floor for that client, not slack.
The Codex target was 2700 while the catalog was counted by user-invocability.
A live probe showed Codex lists by agents/openai.yaml policy instead, so it
sees the same six routers as every other client and carries the same target.
largest_body_bytes_max is the Agent Skills guidance of a body under
5000 tokens, expressed in bytes and rounded to 6 KiB. Phase 1 splits
every agent to meet it; Phase 2 makes the splits semantic.
codex_catalog_chars_max is Codex's hard 2 percent catalog cap.
dispatch_tokens_max is the router-side cost of dispatching one
specialist: a pointer prompt, not a pasted body.
